title: Identification of a novel conserved B-cell epitope in the glycoprotein of rabies virus.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify a novel conserved B-cell epitope in the glycoprotein of rabies virus (RABV) to inform the design of next-generation vaccines and diagnostic tools. This was necessary to address the need for more effective medical countermeasures against rabies, a globally significant zoonotic disease.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the preparation of two monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) using hybridoma cell technology and their validation through i-ELISA, IFA, and Western blot. The research was conducted on RABV glycoprotein samples from diverse genotypes.
analysis.methods: Two mAbs were generated and their specificity and reactivity were validated using i-ELISA, IFA, and Western blot. Epitope mapping was performed using truncated G protein fragments, and alanine-scanning mutagenesis was used to define core binding residues. Bioinformatic analysis and homology modeling were also employed.
analysis.main_results: Two mAbs (1G2 and 4E5) recognized a minimal linear epitope (AEDFVEVHLP) in the G protein of RABV. Bioinformatic analysis revealed highly conserved substitutions of this epitope across diverse RABV genotypes. The epitope was localized to a solvent-exposed α-helical conformation on the G protein surface.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study identified a novel, highly conserved linear B-cell epitope on the RABV glycoprotein, providing a precise molecular target for the rational design of next-generation vaccines and diagnostic tools.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of more effective vaccines and diagnostic tools for rabies, a globally significant zoonotic disease.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the use of a limited number of genotypes and the need for further validation in a broader range of RABV strains. The evidence strength is moderate due to the limited sample size and the need for additional studies to confirm the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study identified a novel, highly conserved linear B-cell epitope in the glycoprotein of rabies virus, providing a precise molecular target for next-generation vaccines and diagnostic tools. title: Immunogenicity of Single-visit, Two-site Intradermal Pre-exposure Rabies Prophylaxis in Children: A Prospective Interventional Study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Rabies remains a major public health concern in endemic countries, particularly among children. However, pediatric data on single-visit, 2-site intradermal pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) regimens remain limited.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This prospective single-arm study enrolled healthy children 1-18 years old at a tertiary care center. The enrolled cohort comprised participants 2-15 years old. Participants received a single-visit, 2-site intradermal rabies PrEP regimen with a Vero cell culture rabies vaccine (RABIVAX-S®).

Participants with rabies virus neutralizing antibody concentrations <0.5 IU/mL at day 28 or day 180 received 2 intradermal booster doses on days 0 and 3 after laboratory results became available and participants returned for follow-up, followed by repeat antibody assessment 7 days after the first booster dose. The primary outcome was seroprotection (≥0.5 IU/mL).
analysis.main_results: Forty-eight children were enrolled, of whom 44 were evaluated on day 28. On day 28, 40/44 (90.9%) achieved protective antibody concentrations (≥0.5 IU/mL). Among 40 participants included in the day 180 analysis, 27 (67.5%) maintained protective concentrations. All participants with insufficient concentrations (n = 4 on day 28, n = 13 on day 180) demonstrated robust anamnestic responses following booster administration, achieving 100% seroprotection within 7 days.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Single-visit, 2-site intradermal rabies PrEP demonstrated high early seroprotection and preserved immunologic priming despite declining antibody concentrations at 6 months. These findings support further evaluation of simplified pediatric PrEP regimens in larger controlled studies.

The primary outcome was seroprotection, defined as antibody concentrations ≥0.5 IU/mL. Forty-eight children were enrolled, with 44 assessed on day 28, where 90.9% achieved protective levels. At day 180, 67.5% maintained these concentrations. All participants with insufficient antibody levels after the initial regimen demonstrated robust anamnestic responses following booster doses, achieving 100% seroprotection within 7 days.
